For each file, find EVERY string that can reach a player's screen, and report it in the structured output. That includes:
- chat/console messages: game.print, player.print, force.print, surface.print
- flying text (player.create_local_flying_text etc.)
- GUI: caption=, tooltip=, text= on LuaGuiElement .add{} or assignments, including strings inside localised-string tables
- commands.add_command name + help text, and every response string those commands print
- custom alerts, message dialogs, set_goal_description, chart/map tag names, anything else display-bound
- data-stage: localised_name/localised_description, prototype names/descriptions, setting prototypes
- error() messages and log() calls (classify as category 'error'/'log', visibility 'log-only' or 'debug' as appropriate)
- strings handed to other mods or external systems (remote interface return values that get displayed, Discord bridge payloads) → category 'external'

Include even tiny strings ("OK", "Cancel", "+", "▶", "×"). For icon/symbol-only strings add hazard 'symbol-only'. Do NOT report: code comments, table keys, event/style/prototype identifier names used only as identifiers, file paths, pattern strings for string.find, storage keys.

- status: 'localised' if it is already a {"section.key", ...} locale reference, 'partial' if a locale reference is concatenated/mixed with hardcoded English, 'hardcoded' otherwise.
- dynamic: describe exactly how it is assembled if not static — every '..' concatenation, string.format, table.concat, tick-to-time formatting, number formatting, player/team name interpolation. This is critical: concatenated sentences are the main localisation hazard.
- visibility: 'player' (any player sees it), 'admin' (admin-only), 'debug' (behind a debug flag), 'external' (leaves the game: Discord, RCON, files), 'log-only'.
- hazards, any of: 'concat' (sentence built by concatenation), 'plural' (text hardcodes singular/plural like "1 slot"/"slots" or picks between them in Lua), 'sentence-fragments' (reusable fragment strings composed into sentences elsewhere), 'rich-text' (embeds [color=]/[item=]/[font=] tags), 'server-side-string' (built into a plain Lua string before display, so all players would get one language), 'discord-mirror' (also sent to Discord/external where a LocalisedString cannot go), 'symbol-only', 'sorted-by-text' (list sorted by the display string), 'newlines' (embedded \n layout).

files_scanned must list every file you read (repo-relative), even ones with zero strings. In notes, mention anything structurally interesting for the localisation plan (helper functions that build messages, message pipelines, patterns repeated across files).

Your final output is consumed by a script, not a human — return only the structured data.

116	-- ═══ Custom Team Settings tabs ════════════════════════════════════════
117	--
118	-- Other mods can add their own tab to the Team Settings panel. They register
119	-- ONCE, in their on_init / on_configuration_changed (where remote.call is
120	-- legal) via:
121	--     remote.call("mts-v1", "register_team_tab",
122	--         { name = "my-mod", caption = "My Mod", order = "z" })
123	-- and listen to the on_team_tab_built event to populate the content frame they
124	-- are handed.
125	--
126	-- The registry lives in `storage` so it survives save/load and is identical on
127	-- every peer. This is what makes the API multiplayer-safe: a client joining
128	-- mid-game (or any reload) can't remote.call in on_load to re-register, so a
129	-- session-scoped registry would be empty on the joiner while populated on the
130	-- host -- a handler-identity mismatch / desync risk. Persisting it sidesteps
131	-- that: the spec is plain data and rides along in the save.
132	local function tab_registry()
133	    storage.mts_custom_tabs = storage.mts_custom_tabs or {}
134	    return storage.mts_custom_tabs
135	end
136	
137	-- Validate a registration spec at the trust boundary (AT-2/AT-3): name must be a
138	-- string; order is coerced to a string/number (a mixed number-vs-string `order`
139	-- across two mods otherwise crashes the sort, and it recurs every session since
140	-- the registry persists); an unusable caption type is dropped (it would crash
141	-- pane.add); and the owning mod is captured so the entry can be swept when that
142	-- mod is removed (see validate_registry). Returns a sanitized entry or nil.
143	local function sanitize_spec(spec)
144	    if type(spec) ~= "table" or type(spec.name) ~= "string" then return nil end
145	    local order = spec.order
146	    if type(order) ~= "string" and type(order) ~= "number" then order = spec.name end
147	    local caption = spec.caption
148	    if caption ~= nil and type(caption) ~= "string"
149	       and type(caption) ~= "number" and type(caption) ~= "table" then
150	        caption = nil
151	    end
152	    return {
153	        name    = spec.name,
154	        caption = caption,
155	        order   = order,
156	        mod     = type(spec.mod) == "string" and spec.mod or nil,
157	    }
158	end
159	
160	-- Sort by order then name, coercing order to string so a legacy mixed-type entry
161	-- can never crash the comparator (defense behind sanitize_spec).
162	local function by_order_then_name(a, b)
163	    local ao, bo = tostring(a.order), tostring(b.order)
164	    if ao ~= bo then return ao < bo end
165	    return a.name < b.name
166	end
167	
168	-- Drop registry entries whose owning mod is no longer active (AT-3). Only
169	-- entries registered WITH a `mod` field are sweepable; entries without one
170	-- persist (a documented requirement for consumers).
171	function remote_api.validate_registry(storage_key)
172	    local t = storage[storage_key]
173	    if not t then return end
174	    for k, def in pairs(t) do
175	        if def.mod and not script.active_mods[def.mod] then t[k] = nil end
176	    end
177	end
178	
179	function remote_api.register_team_tab(spec)
180	    local e = sanitize_spec(spec)
181	    if not e then return end
182	    e.caption = e.caption or e.name
183	    tab_registry()[e.name] = e
184	end
185	
186	--- Registered custom tabs, sorted by order then name.
187	function remote_api.get_team_tabs()
188	    local list = {}
189	    for _, def in pairs(tab_registry()) do list[#list + 1] = def end
190	    table.sort(list, by_order_then_name)
191	    return list
192	end
193	
194	-- ═══ Custom welcome-screen tabs ═══════════════════════════════════════
195	--
196	-- Same contract as the team tabs above, for the centered welcome screen. A
197	-- downstream mod (e.g. a scenario like Expanse) registers ONCE in its on_init /
198	-- on_configuration_changed via:
199	--     remote.call("mts-v1", "register_welcome_tab",
200	--         { name = "my-mod", caption = "My Mod", order = "a" })
201	-- and listens to on_welcome_tab_built to fill the content frame it is handed.
202	-- Registered tabs render BEFORE MTS's own About/Discord and the first is
203	-- selected by default, so the host scenario leads the welcome screen. Registry
204	-- lives in storage for the same multiplayer-safe reason as the team tabs.
205	local function welcome_tab_registry()

207	    return storage.mts_welcome_tabs
208	end

212	    if not e then return end
213	    e.caption = e.caption or e.name
214	    welcome_tab_registry()[e.name] = e
215	end

220	    for _, def in pairs(welcome_tab_registry()) do list[#list + 1] = def end
221	    table.sort(list, by_order_then_name)
222	    return list

524	-- ═══ on_player_changed_force adapter ══════════════════════════════════
525	--
526	-- Called from control.lua's on_player_changed_force handler. Translates
527	-- a single Factorio event into the appropriate join/leave raises so the
528	-- buddy-join flow, /mts-rejoin, and admin force moves are all covered
529	-- automatically — callers don't have to remember to fire these.
530	
531	-- The type()-guarded team-force predicate now lives in helpers (AT-1 boundary
532	-- safety travels with it). Aliased locally so this module's many call sites and
533	-- the trust-boundary intent read unchanged.
534	local is_team_force_name = helpers.is_team_force

536	function remote_api.on_player_changed_force(event)
537	    local old_name = event.force and event.force.name
538	    local player   = game.get_player(event.player_index)
539	    local new_name = player and player.force and player.force.name
540	    local old_team = is_team_force_name(old_name)
541	    local new_team = is_team_force_name(new_name)
542	
543	    -- Always fire the frozen mts-v1 script events for third-party mods (both halves of a
544	    -- switch). These no longer auto-bridge; the bridge presentation is decided below.
545	    if old_team then remote_api.raise_player_left_team(event.player_index, old_name) end
546	    if new_team then remote_api.raise_player_joined_team(event.player_index, new_name) end
547	
548	    -- Suppress bridge messages when the player is temporarily on the spectator force due to
549	    -- the spectate-another-surface feature. spectator_real_force is set before the force
550	    -- change and cleared after restore, so its presence here reliably identifies a
551	    -- spectate hop vs. a real landing-pen join/leave.
552	    local sf = storage.spectator_real_force
553	    local is_spectator_hop = sf and sf[event.player_index] ~= nil
554	        and (new_name == "spectator" or old_name == "spectator")
555	    if is_spectator_hop then return end
556	
557	    -- Bridge presentation: one deduped sentence per force change.
558	    local who = player and player.name or ("player " .. event.player_index)
559	    if old_team and new_team then
560	        -- Mid-game switch between two teams → a single "switched" line.
561	        remote_api.emit_to_bridge("mts.player_switched_team", {
562	            player = who,
563	            from   = helpers.team_display(old_name),
564	            to     = helpers.team_display(new_name),
565	            text   = string.format("%s switched to %s", who, helpers.team_display(new_name)),
566	        })
567	    elseif new_team then
568	        -- Joined a team from a non-team force. The initial auto-claim on connect
569	        -- coincides with the mts.player_joined connect message, so it's suppressed
570	        -- (flag set by the lifecycle handler); deliberate later joins still announce.
571	        local suppress = storage.odb_suppress_claim
572	        if suppress and suppress[event.player_index] then
573	            suppress[event.player_index] = nil
574	        else
575	            remote_api.emit_to_bridge("mts.player_joined_team", {
576	                player = who,
577	                team   = helpers.team_display(new_name),
578	                text   = string.format("%s joined %s", who, helpers.team_display(new_name)),
579	            })
580	        end
581	    elseif old_team then
582	        -- Left a team to a non-team force (e.g. spectator). Disconnects don't reach
583	        -- here (disconnecting doesn't change force) — those go through mts.player_left.
584	        remote_api.emit_to_bridge("mts.player_left_team", {
585	            player = who,
586	            team   = helpers.team_display(old_name),
587	            text   = string.format("%s left %s", who, helpers.team_display(old_name)),
588	        })
589	    end
590	end

741	-- Ensure a hidden, powerless, non-charting passive radar exists at `position`
742	-- on `surface` (name, index, or LuaSurface) owned by `force_name`, so the
743	-- surface stays live-viewable for spectators even when no team member stands on
744	-- it. The radar's constantly-revealed ring belongs to the team force, so it is
745	-- shared to chart-sharing spectators with no power draw and no map charting
746	-- (see prototypes/entities/passive-radar.lua). Idempotent per (surface,
747	-- position): a repeat call returns the existing radar rather than stacking
748	-- duplicates -- so consumers safely re-call it after every surface clone (which
749	-- gives the radar a new unit_number on a new surface) and place several at
750	-- different coordinates to cover a base larger than one ring. Returns the
751	-- LuaEntity (all mods share one Lua state, so the reference is valid for the
752	-- caller) or nil if the surface/force is invalid.
753	local PASSIVE_RADAR_NAME = "mts-passive-radar"
754	local function resolve_surface(surface_ref)
755	    local t = type(surface_ref)
756	    if t == "string" or t == "number" then
757	        return game.surfaces[surface_ref]
758	    end
759	    -- LuaSurface passed directly (same Lua state across mods). A LuaObject's type()
760	    -- is engine-dependent (table or userdata), so don't gate on it -- just probe
761	    -- object_name behind a pcall in case it's some unrelated value.
762	    if t == "table" or t == "userdata" then
763	        local ok, on = pcall(function() return surface_ref.object_name end)
764	        if ok and on == "LuaSurface" then return surface_ref end
765	    end
766	    return nil
767	end
768	local function ensure_passive_radar_impl(force_name, surface_ref, position)
769	    local force = type(force_name) == "string" and game.forces[force_name]
770	    if not (force and force.valid) then return nil end
771	    local surface = resolve_surface(surface_ref)
772	    if not (surface and surface.valid) then return nil end
773	    -- Shape-guard position: a non-table (number/string) would error in the engine
774	    -- find_entities_filtered / create_entity calls below (AT-5).
775	    if type(position) ~= "table" then position = {x = 0, y = 0} end
776	
777	    -- Re-assert ownership + the inert flags on every call. A radar carried across
778	    -- a surface clone can come back with default flags (destructible true), so we
779	    -- harden on the found path too, not just on create.
780	    local function harden(radar)
781	        if not (radar and radar.valid) then return nil end
782	        if radar.force ~= force then radar.force = force end
783	        radar.destructible = false
784	        radar.operable     = false
785	        radar.minable      = false
786	        return radar
787	    end
788	
789	    -- Idempotent: reuse a passive radar already at this spot. find_entity is
790	    -- unreliable here (the radar has a zero collision box), so match by position.
791	    local found = surface.find_entities_filtered{name = PASSIVE_RADAR_NAME, position = position, radius = 1}
792	    if found[1] and found[1].valid then return harden(found[1]) end
793	
794	    return harden(surface.create_entity{name = PASSIVE_RADAR_NAME, position = position, force = force})
795	end

4	--
5	-- Runtime detection for the Space Age DLC and shared helpers for naming
6	-- and enumerating planets. Used by both the data stage (prototypes/) and
7	-- runtime (scripts/, compat/) to agree on the same planet set.
8	--
9	-- Planet enumeration philosophy
10	-- ─────────────────────────────
11	-- Earlier versions hardcoded BASE_PLANETS = {"nauvis", "vulcanus", ...}.
12	-- That excluded modded planets (Maraxsis, Lignumis, Muluna, etc.) from
13	-- variant creation, force locks, and discovery-tech routing. We now
14	-- enumerate dynamically:
15	--
16	--   • At data stage: iterate `data.raw.planet`. Any mod-registered planet
17	--     present by data-final-fixes (MTS's enumeration point) is included.
18	--     Mods that depend on a planet library (e.g. PlanetsLib) typically
19	--     register through that library, which ultimately calls data:extend.
20	--     To guarantee load order, MTS lists popular planet libraries as
21	--     optional dependencies in info.json so their data stages run first.
22	--
23	--   • At runtime: iterate `game.planets`. This is the canonical accessor
24	--     for planet prototypes in 2.0; it includes every planet Factorio
25	--     currently considers registered, regardless of how it got there.
26	--
27	-- Both iterators skip MTS's own per-team variants (anything matching the
28	-- "mts-<base>-<slot>" pattern) so we don't recursively treat our variants
29	-- as base planets and create variants-of-variants.
30	
31	local space_age = {}
32	
33	--- Return true if Space Age is loaded. We detect it by checking
34	--- `game.planets` which is always a valid LuaCustomTable but only non-empty
35	--- when Space Age registers planet prototypes. Team Starts uses this same
36	--- pattern (they don't touch `prototypes.planet` at all at runtime).
37	local cached_active
38	function space_age.is_active()
39	    if cached_active ~= nil then return cached_active end
40	
41	    -- Detect from active_mods ALONE. It is available and identical on every peer
42	    -- at every stage; Space Age being loaded guarantees its planet prototypes
43	    -- exist, so the old secondary `game.planets` probe added no determinism but
44	    -- DID introduce a hazard: a call while `game == nil` cached a permanent wrong
45	    -- `false` on that peer, which could diverge from a peer that cached `true`.
46	    cached_active = script.active_mods["space-age"] ~= nil
47	    log("[multi-team-support] Space Age detection: active=" .. tostring(cached_active))
48	    return cached_active
49	end
50	
51	--- Clear the cached detection result (used on_configuration_changed).
52	function space_age.invalidate_cache()
53	    cached_active = nil
54	end
55	
56	--- Canonical name for a per-team planet variant.
57	---   variant_name("nauvis", 1) -> "mts-nauvis-1"
58	function space_age.variant_name(base, team_slot)
59	    return string.format("mts-%s-%d", base, team_slot)
60	end
61	
62	--- Parse a variant name back into (base, team_slot), or nil if not a variant.
63	--- The base capture accepts hyphens and underscores so modded planets with
64	--- names like "muluna-2" or "alien_world" still parse correctly.
65	function space_age.parse_variant(name)
66	    local base, slot = name:match("^mts%-(.+)%-(%d+)$")
67	    if not base then return nil end
68	    return base, tonumber(slot)
69	end
70	
71	--- Return true when `name` is one of MTS's per-team variants. Used by
72	--- the iteration helpers below to avoid recursively treating our own
73	--- variants as base planets.
74	local function is_variant_name(name)
75	    return name and name:find("^mts%-") ~= nil
76	end
77	
78	-- ═══ Planet enumeration ════════════════════════════════════════════════
79	--
80	-- These two helpers are the canonical source for "what base planets do we
81	-- know about?". Use list_base_planets_data() at the data stage (typically
82	-- data-final-fixes) and list_base_planets_runtime() in control-stage code
83	-- (on_init, on_configuration_changed, event handlers).
84	--
85	-- Both return a sorted-by-name list so iteration order is deterministic
86	-- across saves — important for desync-sensitive multiplayer code that
87	-- builds storage tables in this order.
88	
89	--- Sorted list of base-planet names available at data stage. Excludes
90	--- MTS's own variants. Safe to call before data-final-fixes runs (any
91	--- planets registered before MTS's iteration point are picked up).
92	function space_age.list_base_planets_data()
93	    local names = {}
94	    if data and data.raw and data.raw.planet then
95	        for name in pairs(data.raw.planet) do
96	            if not is_variant_name(name) then
97	                names[#names + 1] = name
98	            end
99	        end
100	    end
101	    table.sort(names)
102	    return names
103	end
104	
105	--- Sorted list of base-planet names available at runtime. Excludes
106	--- MTS's own variants. Reflects the actual planet prototypes Factorio
107	--- has loaded — modded planets registered via any path (data:extend,
108	--- PlanetsLib:extend, etc.) end up here.
109	function space_age.list_base_planets_runtime()
110	    local names = {}
111	    if game and game.planets then
112	        for name in pairs(game.planets) do
113	            if not is_variant_name(name) then
114	                names[#names + 1] = name
115	            end
116	        end
117	    end
118	    table.sort(names)
119	    return names
120	end
121	
122	return space_age

23	--- Opt a surface out of (or back into) the default spawn label. A consumer mod
24	--- that renders its own richer label on a surface it owns (e.g. Expanse, which

27	--- reused surface index can't carry a stale flag. Destroys any label already drawn.
28	function spawn_labels.set_enabled(surface_name, enabled)
29	    if type(surface_name) ~= "string" then return end
30	    storage.spawn_labels_disabled = storage.spawn_labels_disabled or {}

37	        if id then

241	--- Remember each connected player's zoom while they are on their OWN view, so
242	--- returning from spectating another team can restore it. There is no
243	--- zoom-changed event and a GPS click flips the zoom before our handlers run,
244	--- so we poll a recent home value instead. Skips foreign remote views (a
245	--- spectate or friend-view) so we never capture the target's zoom.
246	function M.track_home_zoom()
247	    storage.spectator_last_zoom = storage.spectator_last_zoom or {}
248	    storage.spectator_last_remote_view = storage.spectator_last_remote_view or {}

255	                foreign = owner ~= nil and owner ~= M.get_effective_force(player)
256	            end
257	            if not foreign then
258	                local ok, zoom = pcall(function() return player.zoom end)
259	                if ok and zoom then storage.spectator_last_zoom[player.index] = zoom end
260	                if in_remote then
261	                    -- Map view of their own base: remember where the camera is
262	                    -- looking, to return there (player.position is the camera

44	--- Wrap a player sitting in Remote View on another team's surface into
45	--- spectate (non-friend) or friend-view (friend). original_controller_type is
46	--- the controller they were in BEFORE the click that brought them here, passed
47	--- through to exit so it restores physical-vs-remote view correctly.
48	local function try_enter_foreign_view(player, original_controller_type)
49	    if player.controller_type ~= defines.controllers.remote then return end
50	    if core.is_spectating(player) then return end
51	    local surface = player.surface
52	    local owner   = surface_utils.get_owner(surface)
53	    if not owner then return end
54	    local viewer_force = game.forces[core.get_effective_force(player)]
55	    local target_force = game.forces[owner]
56	    if not (viewer_force and target_force and viewer_force ~= target_force) then return end
57	    local position = player.position
58	    if core.needs_spectator_mode(viewer_force, target_force) then
59	        ops.enter_from_remote(player, target_force, surface, position, original_controller_type)
60	    else
61	        ops.enter_friend_view(player, surface, position)

65	--- Detects GPS/map-click entry into remote view on a foreign surface and
66	--- wraps the player in spectate mode; also detects remote-view exit.
67	function M.on_controller_changed(player, old_controller_type)
68	    -- Case 1: entered remote view from a non-remote controller (clicking a
69	    -- GPS while on the character). old_controller_type is the pre-click
70	    -- controller — used to restore physical-vs-remote view on exit.
71	    if player.controller_type == defines.controllers.remote
72	       and old_controller_type ~= defines.controllers.remote then
73	        try_enter_foreign_view(player, old_controller_type)
74	
75	    -- Case 2: exited remote view while spectating.
76	    elseif old_controller_type == defines.controllers.remote
77	       and player.controller_type ~= defines.controllers.remote
78	       and core.is_spectating(player) then
79	        log("[multi-team-support:spectator] on_controller_changed: " .. player.name
80	            .. " exited remote view, restoring force")
81	        ops.exit(player)
82	    end
83	
84	    -- Track the settled controller type so on_player_changed_surface can tell a
85	    -- GPS click made from INSIDE remote view (surface changes, controller type
86	    -- does not — never fires this event) from a transition INTO remote view
87	    -- (handled above). This makes the surface-handler entry order-independent.
88	    storage.spectator_prev_controller = storage.spectator_prev_controller or {}
89	    storage.spectator_prev_controller[player.index] = player.controller_type
90	end
91	
92	--- Auto-exit when the spectated camera moves off the target's surfaces.
93	--- Handles the case where pressing Escape in a spectator session reverts
94	--- the camera to the player's own physical surface without firing
95	--- on_player_controller_changed, leaving them stuck in spectator mode.
96	function M.on_player_changed_surface(player)
97	    if not (player and player.valid) then return end
98	
99	    if not core.is_spectating(player) then
100	        -- A GPS click made from INSIDE remote view (map already open, or a
101	        -- second GPS) moves the camera onto a new surface WITHOUT changing the
102	        -- controller type, so on_controller_changed never fires. For a foreign
103	        -- team that needs spectator mode, wrap it here — otherwise the player
104	        -- sits on their own force viewing a hidden surface: a permanent black
105	        -- screen that only clears by Esc-ing to the character and re-clicking.
106	        --
107	        -- prev == remote proves they were ALREADY in remote view, so (a) the
108	        -- controller to restore on exit is remote, and (b) this is genuinely a
109	        -- surface-only change, not a character->remote transition (which
110	        -- on_controller_changed owns, with the correct pre-click controller).
111	        -- Friends are left alone: their surface is visible, so the native view
112	        -- already works and needs no force swap.
113	        local prev = (storage.spectator_prev_controller or {})[player.index]
114	        if player.controller_type == defines.controllers.remote
115	           and prev == defines.controllers.remote then
116	            local owner = surface_utils.get_owner(player.surface)
117	            if owner then
118	                local viewer_force = game.forces[core.get_effective_force(player)]
119	                local target_force = game.forces[owner]
120	                if viewer_force and target_force and viewer_force ~= target_force
121	                   and core.needs_spectator_mode(viewer_force, target_force) then
122	                    ops.enter_from_remote(player, target_force, player.surface,
123	                        player.position, defines.controllers.remote)
124	                end
125	            end
126	        end
127	        return
128	    end
129	
130	    local target_force_name = storage.spectating_target[player.index]
131	    if not target_force_name then return end
132	
133	    local owner = surface_utils.get_owner(player.surface)
134	    if owner == target_force_name then return end
135	
136	    log("[multi-team-support:spectator] on_player_changed_surface: "
137	        .. player.name .. " camera left target force territory ("
138	        .. target_force_name .. " → "
139	        .. (owner or "<unowned>")
140	        .. " on " .. player.surface.name .. "), auto-exiting spectator")
141	    ops.exit(player)
142	end

144	--- Handle friendship changes for active spectators/friend-viewers.
145	function M.on_friend_changed(player_force, target_force, is_friend)

147	        .. player_force.name .. (is_friend and " friended " or " unfriended ")
148	        .. target_force.name)
149	
150	    if is_friend then
151	        for idx, spectated_fn in pairs(storage.spectating_target) do
152	            if spectated_fn == player_force.name
153	               and storage.spectator_real_force[idx] == target_force.name then
154	                local p = game.get_player(idx)
155	                if p and p.connected then upgrade_to_friend_view(p, idx) end
156	            end
157	        end
158	    else
159	        for _, p in pairs(target_force.connected_players) do
160	            if p.controller_type == defines.controllers.remote then
161	                local owner = surface_utils.get_owner(p.surface)
162	                if owner == player_force.name then
163	                    downgrade_to_spectator(p, player_force)
164	                end
165	            end
166	        end
167	    end
168	end

170	function M.on_player_left(player)
171	    if not core.is_spectating(player) then return end
172	    log("[multi-team-support:spectator] on_player_left: restoring " .. player.name)
173	    core.restore_player_state(player)
174	    core.clear_spectator_storage(player.index)
175	    core.update_spectator_surfaces()
176	end
177	
178	function M.on_player_joined(player)
179	    local real_fn = storage.spectator_real_force[player.index]
180	
181	    if real_fn then
182	        local was_on_spectator = (player.force.name == "spectator")
183	        core.restore_player_state(player)
184	        core.clear_spectator_storage(player.index)
185	        core.update_spectator_surfaces()
186	        if was_on_spectator then
187	            log("[multi-team-support:spectator] on_player_joined: restored " .. player.name
188	                .. " from spectator force")
189	        else
190	            log("[multi-team-support:spectator] on_player_joined: cleaned stale storage for "
191	                .. player.name)
192	        end
193	        return
194	    end
195	
196	    -- Defensive cleanup: fix leftover spectator permission group or negative
197	    -- crafting modifier from a previous session where storage was cleared
198	    -- without restoring state.
199	    if player.force.name ~= "spectator" then
200	        local pg = player.permission_group
201	        if pg and pg.name == "spectator" then
202	            local default_group = game.permissions.get_group("Default")
203	            if default_group then default_group.add_player(player) end
204	            log("[multi-team-support:spectator] on_player_joined: fixed leftover spectator"
205	                .. " permission group for " .. player.name)
206	        end
207	        if player.character and player.character_crafting_speed_modifier < 0 then
208	            player.character_crafting_speed_modifier = 0
209	            log("[multi-team-support:spectator] on_player_joined: reset negative crafting"
210	                .. " modifier for " .. player.name)
211	        end
212	    end
213	end
214	
215	-- ─── Chat ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
216	
217	function M.get_chat_prefix(player)
218	    local target_fn = core.get_target(player)
219	    if target_fn then
220	        return "[on " .. helpers.display_name(target_fn) .. "'s base][spectator] "
221	    end
222	    if player.controller_type == defines.controllers.remote then
223	        local owner = surface_utils.get_owner(player.surface)
224	        if owner and owner ~= player.force.name then
225	            return "[on " .. helpers.display_name(owner) .. "'s base][friend] "
226	        end
227	    end
228	    return ""
229	end
230	
231	return M

2	-- Public spectation operations: enter, exit, switch, friend-view.
3	
4	local helpers       = require("scripts.helpers")
5	local surface_utils = require("scripts.surface_utils")
6	local core          = require("scripts.spectator.core")
7	
8	local M = {}
9	
10	function M.enter(player, target_force, surface, position, target_player)
11	    log("[multi-team-support:spectator] enter: " .. player.name
12	        .. " → " .. target_force.name
13	        .. " on " .. surface.name
14	        .. " at " .. serpent.line(position))
15	
16	    -- Save pre-spectate location. Use physical_position/surface because
17	    -- player.position is the camera position when already in map view.
18	    if not core.is_spectating(player) then
19	        storage.spectator_saved_location[player.index] = {
20	            surface_name    = player.physical_surface.name,
21	            position        = {x = player.physical_position.x, y = player.physical_position.y},
22	            controller_type = player.controller_type,
23	            -- hub is non-nil when the player is sitting in a space platform hub.
24	            -- enter_space_platform() is needed on exit to restore the pilot
25	            -- relationship (set_controller alone doesn't).
26	            was_in_hub      = player.hub ~= nil,
27	            -- The GUI spectate button fires before the view changes, so the
28	            -- live zoom is still the home zoom.
29	            zoom            = (function() local ok, z = pcall(function() return player.zoom end) return ok and z or nil end)(),
30	        }
31	    end
32	
33	    helpers.diag("spectator.enter: BEFORE state changes", player)
34	    storage.spectating_target[player.index] = target_force.name
35	    core.apply_spectator_state(player)
36	    helpers.diag("spectator.enter: AFTER apply_spectator_state", player)
37	    core.open_remote_view(player, surface, position)
38	    helpers.diag("spectator.enter: AFTER open_remote_view", player)
39	    core.announce_spectation(player, target_force, true, target_player, surface)
40	    core.update_spectator_surfaces()
41	
42	    log("[multi-team-support:spectator] enter: done, force=" .. player.force.name)
43	end
44	
45	function M.exit(player)
46	    if not core.is_spectating(player) then return end
47	    log("[multi-team-support:spectator] exit: " .. player.name)
48	    helpers.diag("spectator.exit: BEFORE restore_player_state", player)
49	
50	    local target_fn       = storage.spectating_target[player.index]
51	    local spectated_surface = player.surface  -- capture before force restore repoints it
52	    core.restore_player_state(player)
53	    helpers.diag("spectator.exit: AFTER restore_player_state", player)
54	
55	    local saved = storage.spectator_saved_location[player.index]
56	    local target_surface, target_pos
57	    local used_fallback = false
58	    if saved then
59	        target_surface = game.surfaces[saved.surface_name]
60	        target_pos     = saved.position
61	    end
62	    if not target_surface then
63	        target_surface = surface_utils.get_home_surface(player.force, player.index)
64	        target_pos     = helpers.ORIGIN
65	        used_fallback  = true
66	    end
67	
68	    if target_surface then
69	        -- Collision avoidance only on the ORIGIN fallback (saved surface deleted or
70	        -- unresolved). Skip on the normal saved-position restore, where the
71	        -- character is still there and find_non_colliding_position would treat it
72	        -- as a blocker. (Was gated on `not saved`, but `saved` stays truthy even
73	        -- when saved.surface_name no longer resolves, so the fallback was skipped.)
74	        if used_fallback and player.character then
75	            local safe = target_surface.find_non_colliding_position(
76	                player.character.name, target_pos, 8, 0.5)
77	            target_pos = safe or target_pos
78	        end
79	        helpers.diag("spectator.exit: TELEPORT → " .. target_surface.name
80	            .. " at " .. string.format("(%.1f,%.1f)", target_pos.x, target_pos.y), player)
81	        player.teleport(target_pos, target_surface)
82	
83	        -- Restore remote view when:
84	        --   1. Player was in remote view before spectating (e.g. sitting in a hub).
85	        --   2. Destination is a space platform (hub-view is the natural state there).
86	        local restore_remote = false
87	        if saved and saved.controller_type == defines.controllers.remote then
88	            restore_remote = true
89	        end
90	        if target_surface.platform then restore_remote = true end
91	
92	        local saved_zoom = saved and saved.zoom
93	        -- Whether we set the view's zoom ourselves. False when control was
94	        -- handed to enter_space_platform (hub view) — Platformer's normal
95	        -- return — where the hub owns its own zoom and we must not touch it.
96	        local applied_zoom = false
97	        if restore_remote then
98	            -- Platform-bound remote (hub) vs position-based remote (planet variant).
99	            -- Use enter_space_platform when available — it restores the pilot
100	            -- relationship; set_controller alone only moves the camera.
101	            local platform = target_surface.platform
102	            local hub_entered = false
103	            if platform and platform.valid
104	               and (saved and saved.was_in_hub or target_surface.platform) then
105	                hub_entered = player.enter_space_platform(platform)
106	            end
107	            if not hub_entered then
108	                -- The camera returns to where the map was looking (saved view
109	                -- position); the character already teleported to its physical
110	                -- spot above and stays there. Falls back to the physical spot.
111	                local cam_surface = (saved and saved.view_surface_name
112	                    and game.surfaces[saved.view_surface_name]) or target_surface
113	                local cam_pos = (saved and saved.view_position) or target_pos
114	                player.set_controller{
115	                    type     = defines.controllers.remote,
116	                    surface  = cam_surface,
117	                    position = cam_pos,
118	                }
119	                -- set_controller's start_zoom only seeds a transition, not the
120	                -- remote view's resting zoom (it opens at the engine default).
121	                -- Set the controller's zoom directly, like the physical path.
122	                if saved_zoom then
123	                    pcall(function() player.zoom = saved_zoom end)
124	                    applied_zoom = true
125	                end
126	            end
127	        elseif saved_zoom then
128	            -- Returned to the physical character view: restore its zoom too.
129	            pcall(function() player.zoom = saved_zoom end)
130	            applied_zoom = true
131	        end
132	        -- Re-apply a few ticks later: the controller change can reset zoom on
133	        -- the frame it settles, so one delayed write makes it stick. Only when
134	        -- we actually set the zoom (never over a hub view).
135	        if applied_zoom then
136	            storage.zoom_apply = storage.zoom_apply or {}
137	            storage.zoom_apply[player.index] = { at = game.tick + 4, zoom = saved_zoom }
138	        end
139	    end
140	    storage.spectator_saved_location[player.index] = nil
141	
142	    if target_fn then
143	        local target_force = game.forces[target_fn]
144	        if target_force then
145	            core.announce_spectation(player, target_force, false, nil, spectated_surface)
146	        end
147	    end
148	
149	    core.clear_spectator_storage(player.index)
150	    core.update_spectator_surfaces()
151	    log("[multi-team-support:spectator] exit: done, force=" .. player.force.name)
152	end
153	
154	--- Exit every player tied to a team whose slot is being disbanded/released:
155	--- members currently spectating AWAY (spectator_real_force == force_name), so
156	--- they are restored to their real force and counted/relocated by the disband
157	--- loop instead of being orphaned; and outside viewers spectating INTO the team
158	--- (spectating_target == force_name), so stale visibility doesn't carry onto the
159	--- recycled slot. M.exit restores force / view and refreshes visibility.
160	function M.exit_all_for_force(force_name)
161	    local reals   = storage.spectator_real_force or {}
162	    local targets = storage.spectating_target or {}
163	    -- Snapshot the indices first; M.exit mutates these tables as it clears state.
164	    local hits = {}
165	    for idx, real in pairs(reals) do
166	        if real == force_name or targets[idx] == force_name then hits[#hits + 1] = idx end
167	    end
168	    for _, idx in ipairs(hits) do
169	        local p = game.get_player(idx)
170	        if p and p.valid then M.exit(p) end
171	    end
172	end
173	
174	function M.switch_target(player, target_force, surface, position, target_player)
175	    log("[multi-team-support:spectator] switch_target: " .. player.name
176	        .. " → " .. target_force.name .. " on " .. surface.name)
177	    storage.spectating_target[player.index] = target_force.name
178	    core.open_remote_view(player, surface, position)
179	    core.announce_spectation(player, target_force, true, target_player, surface)
180	    core.update_spectator_surfaces()
181	end
182	
183	--- Like enter() but skips set_controller — used when the engine already moved
184	--- the player into remote view (GPS click, map click on a foreign surface).
185	--- original_controller_type is the controller the player was in BEFORE the
186	--- click. The click has already flipped player.controller_type to remote by
187	--- now, so reading it here would always record "remote" and exit would always
188	--- restore remote view; the caller supplies the real pre-click value so exit
189	--- restores physical view for a click made from the character.
190	function M.enter_from_remote(player, target_force, surface, position, original_controller_type)
191	    log("[multi-team-support:spectator] enter_from_remote: " .. player.name
192	        .. " → " .. target_force.name
193	        .. " on " .. surface.name
194	        .. " at " .. serpent.line(position))
195	
196	    if not core.is_spectating(player) then
197	        -- For a click made from inside the map (remote controller), the camera
198	        -- should return to where it was looking, not the character's physical
199	        -- spot — use the polled map-view position (the GPS click already moved
200	        -- the camera off our base before we run).
201	        local rv = (original_controller_type == defines.controllers.remote)
202	            and storage.spectator_last_remote_view
203	            and storage.spectator_last_remote_view[player.index]
204	        storage.spectator_saved_location[player.index] = {
205	            surface_name      = player.physical_surface.name,
206	            position          = {x = player.physical_position.x, y = player.physical_position.y},
207	            controller_type   = original_controller_type or player.controller_type,
208	            was_in_hub        = player.hub ~= nil,
209	            -- The GPS click already flipped the zoom, so use the polled
210	            -- home-view value (core.track_home_zoom) rather than the live one.
211	            zoom              = (storage.spectator_last_zoom or {})[player.index],
212	            view_surface_name = rv and rv.surface_name or nil,
213	            view_position     = rv and rv.position or nil,
214	        }
215	    end
216	    storage.spectating_target[player.index] = target_force.name
217	    core.apply_spectator_state(player)
218	    core.announce_spectation(player, target_force, true, nil, surface)
219	    core.update_spectator_surfaces()
220	
221	    log("[multi-team-support:spectator] enter_from_remote: done, force=" .. player.force.name)
222	end
223	
224	--- Open a friend-view: direct remote view without spectator force swap.
225	--- When target_force and target_player are both given, broadcasts the
226	--- announcement (follow-cam expand). Other callers suppress it.
227	function M.enter_friend_view(player, surface, position, target_force, target_player)
228	    log("[multi-team-support:spectator] enter_friend_view: " .. player.name
229	        .. " on " .. surface.name)
230	    -- Save pre-view location. Use physical_position/surface for the same
231	    -- reason as enter(): player.position is camera pos in map view.
232	    if not core.is_spectating(player)
233	       and not storage.spectator_saved_location[player.index] then
234	        storage.spectator_saved_location[player.index] = {
235	            surface_name    = player.physical_surface.name,
236	            position        = {x = player.physical_position.x, y = player.physical_position.y},
237	            controller_type = player.controller_type,
238	            was_in_hub      = player.hub ~= nil,
239	        }
240	    end
241	    core.open_remote_view(player, surface, position)
242	    if target_force and target_player then
243	        core.announce_spectation(player, target_force, true, target_player, surface)
244	    end
245	end

2	-- Author: bits-orio

4	--
5	-- Surface ownership queries, visibility management, and chart cleanup.
6	-- Extracted from spectator.lua — these are surface-level concerns, not
7	-- spectator-specific.
8	
9	local helpers = require("scripts.helpers")
10	
11	local surface_utils = {}
12	
13	-- Extract the base planet name from a team surface name, or nil if it isn't
14	-- a team variant. Recognizes "mts-<planet>-<N>" (Space Age) and
15	-- "team-<N>-<planet>" (base 2.0 clone).
16	local function variant_base_planet(name)
17	    if type(name) ~= "string" then return nil end
18	    return name:match("^mts%-(.+)%-%d+$") or name:match("^team%-%d+%-(.+)$")
19	end
20	
21	-- Deterministic seed per base planet, so every team's variant of that planet
22	-- generates identical terrain reflecting the host's chosen map seed.
23	-- Reads the base surface's seed directly when it exists (nauvis always does).
24	-- Outer planet base surfaces are lazy (created on first visit), so fall back
25	-- to nauvis's seed which equals the game's chosen map seed.
26	local function seed_for_base(base)
27	    local base_surface = game.surfaces[base]
28	    if base_surface and base_surface.valid then
29	        return base_surface.map_gen_settings.seed
30	    end
31	    local nauvis = game.surfaces["nauvis"]
32	    return nauvis and nauvis.map_gen_settings.seed or 0
33	end
34	
35	--- The planet a surface REPRESENTS: its engine planet when set, else the
36	--- base planet its team-variant name derives from ("mts-<planet>-<N>" /
37	--- "team-<N>-<planet>"), else nil. Generic surface-identity query for
38	--- consumers (exposed on mts-v1 as get_surface_planet).
39	function surface_utils.represented_planet(surface)
40	    if not surface or not surface.valid then return nil end
41	    if surface.planet then return surface.planet.name end
42	    return variant_base_planet(surface.name)
43	end
44	
45	--- Given a surface, return the force name that owns it, or nil.
46	function surface_utils.get_owner(surface)
47	    if not surface or not surface.valid then return nil end
48	
49	    -- Consumer-registered ephemeral surfaces (mts-v1 create_team_surface). This
50	    -- map is keyed 1:1 by surface name and is immune to planet_map.build(), so it
51	    -- survives on_configuration_changed. Checked first as the most exact record.
52	    local override = (storage.surface_owner_overrides or {})[surface.name]
53	    if override and game.forces[override] then return override end
54	
55	    -- Space Age: per-team planet variants have their own surfaces named
56	    -- after the planet (e.g. "mts-nauvis-1"). The planet_map keeps a
57	    -- reverse lookup built at on_init. O(1), so checked before the O(forces x
58	    -- platforms) scan below -- this is the common case for a variant surface.
59	    local by_planet = (storage.map_planet_to_force or {})[surface.name]
60	    if by_planet and game.forces[by_planet] then
61	        return by_planet
62	    end
63	
64	    -- Fallback (non-Space-Age): cloned surfaces named "team-N-planet". Use a
65	    -- permissive suffix (.+, matching variant_base_planet above) so planet names
66	    -- containing '-' or '_' (e.g. team-1-neo-nauvis) still resolve. O(1) name
67	    -- match, so it also precedes the platforms scan.
68	    local force_name = surface.name:match("^(team%-%d+)%-.+$")
69	    if force_name and game.forces[force_name] then
70	        return force_name
71	    end
72	
73	    -- Space platforms owned by team forces. O(forces x platforms), so LAST: a
74	    -- platform surface carries no name-based record, making this the only branch
75	    -- that can resolve it -- but a planet-variant/clone surface (the common case)
76	    -- never reaches here, having matched an O(1) lookup above (PF-7).
77	    for _, force in pairs(game.forces) do
78	        if force.name:find("^team%-") then
79	            for _, plat in pairs(force.platforms) do
80	                if plat.surface and plat.surface.valid
81	                   and plat.surface.index == surface.index then
82	                    return force.name
83	                end
84	            end
85	        end
86	    end
87	
88	    return nil
89	end
90	
91	--- All surfaces currently owned by a force (by force name), as LuaSurface
92	--- objects. Shared by the production-stat pollers (milestones, stats GUI) and
93	--- the pause wire-reconnect index so they scan a team's own 1-3 surfaces
94	--- instead of every surface in the game (PF-1/PF-2/PF-10). Recomputed each call
95	--- since ownership shifts as surfaces are created/retired; a caller that polls
96	--- repeatedly within one pass should cache the result itself.
97	function surface_utils.owned_surfaces_by_force(force_name)
98	    local out = {}
99	    for _, surface in pairs(game.surfaces) do
100	        if surface.valid and surface_utils.get_owner(surface) == force_name then
101	            out[#out + 1] = surface
102	        end
103	    end
104	    return out
105	end
106	
107	--- Pin a team variant surface to a per-base-planet seed so every team's copy
108	--- of that planet generates identical terrain natively. MUST be called from
109	--- on_surface_created, before any chunk generates. No-op for non-variant
110	--- surfaces. Harmless on nauvis variants (those are clone-mirrored, so the
111	--- clone overwrites generation anyway); it matters for the natively-generated
112	--- outer planets (vulcanus, gleba, …) where terrain isn't cloned.
113	function surface_utils.normalize_variant_seed(surface)
114	    if not (surface and surface.valid) then return end
115	    local base = variant_base_planet(surface.name)
116	    if not base then return end
117	    local mgs = surface.map_gen_settings
118	    local seed = seed_for_base(base)
119	    if mgs.seed == seed then return end
120	    mgs.seed = seed
121	    surface.map_gen_settings = mgs
122	end
123	
124	--- Find a player's home surface, preferring their actual primary
125	--- surface (planet variant or cloned nauvis) over any incidental
126	--- space platform the team might own.
127	---
128	--- Lookup order:
129	---   1. storage.player_surfaces[player_index]: the surface the player
130	---      spawned on. This is their canonical home for vanilla, voidblock,
131	---      Space Age (mts-nauvis-N), and Platformer (platform-N) — every
132	---      mode populates this entry during setup_player_surface.
133	---   2. Space Age home planet variant via map_force_to_planets: covers
134	---      buddies who joined an existing team and don't have their own
135	---      player_surfaces entry but should land on the team's nauvis
136	---      variant.
137	---   3. Surface-name search for any surface owned by this force: another
138	---      buddy fallback for non-Space-Age modes.
139	---   4. Any space platform owned by the force: last-resort fallback for
140	---      the rare case where a team has launched a platform but somehow
141	---      has no other surface (e.g. all planet surfaces deleted, or a
142	---      legacy save state we didn't anticipate).
143	---
144	--- Why platforms are now last
145	--- ──────────────────────────
146	--- Earlier versions returned a space platform first if any existed.
147	--- That made sense for Platformer mode (where the platform IS the
148	--- primary base) but broke for Space Age: any team that had ever
149	--- launched a rocket would have "return to base" send the player to
150	--- the platform instead of their planet. The Platformer case is still
151	--- handled correctly by step 1, because Platformer's setup_player_surface
152	--- populates player_surfaces with the platform's surface name.
153	function surface_utils.get_home_surface(force, player_index)
154	    -- 1. Player's stored home surface (set during setup_player_surface
155	    -- in vanilla / voidblock / platformer / Space Age compat).
156	    local ps = storage.player_surfaces and storage.player_surfaces[player_index]
157	    if ps then
158	        local s = game.surfaces[ps.name]
159	        if s and s.valid then return s end
160	    end
161	
162	    -- 2. Space Age home planet variant: handles buddies on a team
163	    -- whose player_surfaces entry was never populated.
164	    local map_entry = (storage.map_force_to_planets or {})[force.name]
165	    if map_entry and map_entry.nauvis then
166	        local s = game.surfaces[map_entry.nauvis]
167	        if s and s.valid then return s end
168	    end
169	
170	    -- 3. Surface-name search for any surface owned by this force.
171	    -- Catches non-Space-Age buddy joins.
172	    for _, surface in pairs(game.surfaces) do
173	        if surface.valid and surface.name:find("^" .. force.name:gsub("%-", "%%-") .. "%-") then
174	            return surface
175	        end
176	    end
177	
178	    -- 4. Last resort: any space platform owned by the force. Reached
179	    -- only when the team has no planet surface and no cloned surface
180	    -- but somehow has a platform — uncommon, but the original behavior
181	    -- did this so we keep it as a fallback to avoid regressions.
182	    for _, plat in pairs(force.platforms) do
183	        if plat.surface and plat.surface.valid then return plat.surface end
184	    end
185	
186	    return nil
187	end
188	
189	--- Update surface visibility between two forces based on friendship.
190	function surface_utils.update_visibility(force_a, force_b, are_friends)
191	    for _, surface in pairs(game.surfaces) do
192	        local owner = surface_utils.get_owner(surface)
193	        if owner == force_a.name then
194	            helpers.set_surface_hidden(force_b, surface, not are_friends)
195	        elseif owner == force_b.name then
196	            helpers.set_surface_hidden(force_a, surface, not are_friends)
197	        end
198	    end
199	end
200	
201	--- Hide a newly created surface from non-owner, non-friend forces.
202	function surface_utils.on_surface_created(surface)
203	    local owner_fn    = surface_utils.get_owner(surface)
204	    if not owner_fn then return end
205	    local owner_force = game.forces[owner_fn]
206	    if not owner_force then return end
207	
208	    for _, force in pairs(game.forces) do
209	        if force.name:find("^team%-") and force.name ~= owner_fn then
210	            local are_friends = force.get_friend(owner_force)
211	                and owner_force.get_friend(force)
212	            helpers.set_surface_hidden(force, surface, not are_friends)
213	        end
214	    end
215	
216	    -- Hide from spectator force unless someone is actively spectating the owner.
217	    local spec = game.forces["spectator"]
218	    if spec then
219	        local spectated = false
220	        if storage.spectating_target then
221	            for _, target_fn in pairs(storage.spectating_target) do
222	                if target_fn == owner_fn then
223	                    spectated = true
224	                    break
225	                end
226	            end
227	        end
228	        helpers.set_surface_hidden(spec, surface, not spectated)
229	    end
230	end
231	
232	--- Periodic chart cleanup: clears spectator force chart data for
233	--- surfaces with no active spectators.
234	function surface_utils.cleanup_charts()
235	    local spec = game.forces["spectator"]
236	    if not spec then return end
237	
238	    local active_surfaces = {}
239	    for _, target_fn in pairs(storage.spectating_target) do
240	        local force = game.forces[target_fn]
241	        if force then
242	            for _, plat in pairs(force.platforms) do
243	                if plat.surface and plat.surface.valid then
244	                    active_surfaces[plat.surface.index] = true
245	                end
246	            end
247	        end
248	    end
249	
250	    for _, surface in pairs(game.surfaces) do
251	        if not active_surfaces[surface.index] then
252	            local owner = surface_utils.get_owner(surface)
253	            if owner and owner ~= "spectator" then
254	                spec.clear_chart(surface)
255	            end
256	        end
257	    end
258	
259	    log("[multi-team-support:spectator] cleanup_charts: cleared inactive surface charts")
260	end
261	
262	return surface_utils
263

1	-- Multi-Team Support - scripts/team_clock.lua
2	-- Author: bits-orio

4	--
5	-- Per-team "online time": wall-clock ticks during which the team had at least
6	-- one connected member. Unlike the team birth clock (storage.team_clock_start),
7	-- this freezes while the whole team is offline, so a team that logs off for the
8	-- night isn't penalised against teams that happen to be online more hours.
9	--
10	-- This is wall-clock-while-online, NOT a sum of per-player online_time: two
11	-- members playing together for an hour is one hour of team progress, not two.
12	--
13	-- Informational only. Awards / records stay on the birth clock (server-elapsed)
14	-- so an offline base that keeps producing can't manufacture an unbeatable time.
15	--
16	-- Event-driven: we stamp `online_since` on the offline→online transition and
17	-- settle the accumulator on the online→offline transition. No per-tick work.
18	--
19	-- Storage shape:
20	--   storage.team_online_ticks[force_name] = accumulated ticks of finished streaks
21	--   storage.team_online_since[force_name] = tick the current streak began, or nil
22	
23	local spectator = require("scripts.spectator")
24	
25	local team_clock = {}
26	
27	function team_clock.init_storage()
28	    storage.team_online_ticks = storage.team_online_ticks or {}
29	    storage.team_online_since = storage.team_online_since or {}
30	end
31	
32	--- Count connected members whose *effective* force is this team, optionally
33	--- excluding one player. Effective force keeps a member who is peeking at the
34	--- spectator force counted under their real team. The exclude is used on
35	--- on_player_left_game, where the engine may or may not have already dropped the
36	--- leaver from connected_players — excluding by index is correct either way.
37	local function online_member_count(force_name, exclude_index)
38	    local n = 0
39	    for _, p in pairs(game.connected_players) do
40	        if p.index ~= exclude_index and spectator.get_effective_force(p) == force_name then
41	            n = n + 1
42	        end
43	    end
44	    return n
45	end
46	
47	--- Recompute a team's online/offline state and settle its accumulator on a
48	--- transition. Call on any join / leave / force-change touching this team.
49	function team_clock.refresh(force_name, exclude_index)
50	    if not (force_name and force_name:find("^team%-")) then return end
51	    team_clock.init_storage()
52	
53	    local online = online_member_count(force_name, exclude_index) > 0
54	    local since  = storage.team_online_since[force_name]
55	
56	    if online and not since then
57	        storage.team_online_since[force_name] = game.tick
58	    elseif (not online) and since then
59	        storage.team_online_ticks[force_name] =
60	            (storage.team_online_ticks[force_name] or 0) + (game.tick - since)
61	        storage.team_online_since[force_name] = nil
62	    end
63	end
64	
65	--- Total online ticks for a team right now: settled streaks plus the live one.
66	function team_clock.online_ticks(force_name)
67	    local total = (storage.team_online_ticks or {})[force_name] or 0
68	    local since = (storage.team_online_since or {})[force_name]
69	    if since then total = total + (game.tick - since) end
70	    return total
71	end
72	
73	--- Begin tracking when a slot is claimed (clock starts at zero; the caller
74	--- follows up with refresh() once the player's force is set, which stamps the
75	--- first online_since).
76	function team_clock.on_claim(force_name)
77	    team_clock.init_storage()
78	    storage.team_online_ticks[force_name] = storage.team_online_ticks[force_name] or 0
79	end
80	
81	--- Drop all online-time state when a slot is released.
82	function team_clock.on_release(force_name)
83	    if storage.team_online_ticks then storage.team_online_ticks[force_name] = nil end
84	    if storage.team_online_since then storage.team_online_since[force_name] = nil end
85	end
86	
87	return team_clock
88

1	-- Multi-Team Support - scripts/team_disband.lua
2	-- Author: bits-orio

4	--
5	-- Implements the mts-v1 `disband_team` action. It lives in its own module so it
6	-- can require both team_slots and landing_pen (which together would form a
7	-- circular require with remote_api) and inject the implementation back into
8	-- remote_api. Nothing else requires this module, so it's a safe leaf.
9	
10	local team_slots  = require("scripts.team_slots")
11	local landing_pen = require("gui.landing_pen")
12	local spectator   = require("scripts.spectator")
13	local remote_api  = require("scripts.remote_api")
14	local helpers     = require("scripts.helpers")
15	
16	--- Disband a team entirely: every member back to the pen, slot freed, surfaces
17	--- cleaned up. Reuses the normal leave flow (remove_from_team disbands + cleans
18	--- up on the last member removed; return_to_pen relocates each player).
19	local function disband(force_name)
20	    if type(force_name) ~= "string" or not force_name:match("^team%-%d+$") then return end
21	    local force = game.forces[force_name]
22	    if not (force and force.valid) then return end
23	
24	    -- Occupancy guard: every team-N force is pre-created and never destroyed, so
25	    -- game.forces[force_name] is valid even for a slot that was never claimed.
26	    -- Without this, disband_team on an unoccupied slot runs cleanup + release and
27	    -- raises a spurious on_team_released (with no matching on_team_created), and a
28	    -- consumer that defensively re-calls disband_team from its on_team_released
29	    -- handler would recurse until the Lua stack overflows. An occupied-but-empty
30	    -- slot (members force-moved away) still passes and is handled below.
31	    local slot = helpers.team_slot(force_name)
32	    if (storage.team_pool or {})[slot] ~= "occupied" then return end
33	
34	    -- Restore any member currently spectating away (so they enter the members
35	    -- list below and are returned to the pen, not orphaned) and exit outside
36	    -- viewers of this team before it is torn down.
37	    spectator.exit_all_for_force(force_name)
38	
39	    local members = {}
40	    for _, p in pairs(force.players) do members[#members + 1] = p end
41	
42	    if #members == 0 then
43	        team_slots.cleanup_force_surfaces(force_name)
44	        team_slots.release_team_slot(force_name)
45	        return
46	    end
47	
48	    for _, p in pairs(members) do
49	        if p and p.valid then
50	            if spectator.is_spectating(p) then spectator.exit(p) end
51	            team_slots.remove_from_team(p)
52	            landing_pen.return_to_pen(p)
53	        end
54	    end
55	end
56	
57	remote_api.disband_impl = disband
58	
59	return { disband = disband }
60

1	-- Multi-Team Support - scripts/team_modifiers.lua
2	-- Author: bits-orio
3	-- License: GPL-3.0-or-later
4	--
5	-- Per-team gameplay modifiers ("team modifiers"), gated behind the
6	-- non_competitive_enabled admin flag. MTS is competitive by default — every
7	-- team plays under identical rules — so modifiers are an explicit, loudly
8	-- announced exception for private servers with mixed-skill groups: every
9	-- change is broadcast, the mode is shown in the HUD and Teams GUI, and
10	-- record announcements are tagged while the mode is on.
11	--
12	-- Modifiers are implemented per-surface (each team owns its surfaces), which
13	-- is why they can differ per team at all. v1 ships peaceful biters only; the
14	-- storage shape and MODIFIERS list are built for more keys later.
15	--
16	-- A team that EVER had a modifier enabled is permanently marked
17	-- non-competitive (storage.team_noncompetitive) — removing the modifier
18	-- doesn't clear the mark; only disbanding the team does. Leaving
19	-- non-competitive mode is blocked while any marked team exists, so a
20	-- bad-faith admin can't briefly handicap a team and flip the server back
21	-- to competitive as if nothing happened.
22	--
23	-- Storage shape:
24	--   storage.team_modifiers[force_name]      = { peaceful = true }  -- absent keys = standard
25	--   storage.team_noncompetitive[force_name] = true                 -- cleared only on release
26	--
27	-- Cycle-safety: requires only leaf modules (helpers, admin_flags,
28	-- surface_utils), so GUI modules, records, and milestones can all require it.
29	
30	local helpers       = require("scripts.helpers")
31	local admin_flags   = require("scripts.admin_flags")
32	local surface_utils = require("scripts.surface_utils")
33	
34	local M = {}
35	
36	-- Shown wherever the mode is surfaced (HUD tag, card lines, admin section).
37	M.MODE_COLOR = {1, 0.65, 0}
38	
39	M.MODIFIERS = {
40	    {
41	        key     = "peaceful",
42	        label   = "Peaceful biters",
43	        short   = "peaceful",
44	        icon    = "[img=entity/small-biter]",
45	        tooltip = "Biters on this team's surfaces never attack first"
46	            .. " (they still defend themselves).",
47	    },
48	}
49	
50	function M.is_active()
51	    return admin_flags.flag("non_competitive_enabled") == true
52	end
53	
54	local function entry(force_name)
55	    return (storage.team_modifiers or {})[force_name]
56	end
57	
58	function M.has(force_name, key)
59	    local e = entry(force_name)
60	    return (e and e[key]) == true
61	end
62	
63	function M.any(force_name)
64	    local e = entry(force_name)
65	    return e ~= nil and next(e) ~= nil
66	end
67	
68	--- True once a team has ever had a modifier enabled. Cleared only on release.
69	function M.is_marked(force_name)
70	    return (storage.team_noncompetitive or {})[force_name] == true
71	end
72	
73	-- ─── Surface application ───────────────────────────────────────────────
74	
75	--- Re-apply this team's modifier state to every surface it owns.
76	local function apply_team(force_name)
77	    local peaceful = M.has(force_name, "peaceful")
78	    for _, surface in ipairs(surface_utils.owned_surfaces_by_force(force_name)) do
79	        surface.peaceful_mode = peaceful
80	    end
81	end
82	
83	--- Apply the owner team's modifiers to a freshly created surface (new planet
84	--- variant, platform, ...). Called from the on_surface_created path.
85	function M.apply_to_surface(surface, owner_force_name)
86	    if not (surface and surface.valid and owner_force_name) then return end
87	    if M.has(owner_force_name, "peaceful") then
88	        surface.peaceful_mode = true
89	    end
90	end
91	
92	-- ─── Mutation ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
93	
94	local function guidance()
95	    return "See the Teams panel or /mts-modifiers for every team's settings."
96	end
97	
98	--- Set one modifier for one team. Admin GUI entry point. No-op (returns
99	--- false) when the mode is off, the force isn't a team, or nothing changes;
100	--- otherwise applies to the team's surfaces and broadcasts the change.
101	function M.set(force_name, key, enabled, admin_player)
102	    if not M.is_active() then return false end
103	    if not helpers.is_team_force(force_name) then return false end
104	    local def
105	    for _, d in ipairs(M.MODIFIERS) do
106	        if d.key == key then def = d; break end
107	    end
108	    if not def then return false end
109	    if M.has(force_name, key) == (enabled == true) then return false end
110	
111	    storage.team_modifiers = storage.team_modifiers or {}
112	    local e = storage.team_modifiers[force_name] or {}
113	    e[key] = (enabled == true) or nil
114	    storage.team_modifiers[force_name] = next(e) and e or nil
115	
116	    -- Enabling any modifier permanently marks the team non-competitive
117	    -- (removing the modifier later does NOT clear the mark; disband does).
118	    local newly_marked = enabled and not M.is_marked(force_name)
119	    if enabled then
120	        storage.team_noncompetitive = storage.team_noncompetitive or {}
121	        storage.team_noncompetitive[force_name] = true
122	    end
123	
124	    apply_team(force_name)
125	
126	    local who = admin_player
127	        and helpers.colored_name(admin_player.name, admin_player.chat_color)
128	        or "Admin"
129	    local msg = "[Admin] " .. who
130	        .. (enabled and " enabled " or " disabled ") .. def.label
131	        .. " for " .. helpers.team_tag_with_leader(force_name)
132	        .. " (non-competitive mode)."
133	    if newly_marked then
134	        msg = msg .. " This team is now marked non-competitive until it disbands."
135	    end
136	    helpers.broadcast(msg .. " " .. guidance())
137	    return true
138	end
139	
140	--- Blocks disabling non-competitive mode while any MARKED team exists:
141	--- returns a reason string naming those teams, or nil when disabling is
142	--- fine (the mode was enabled by accident and no team ever got a
143	--- modifier). Marked teams block even with their modifiers since removed —
144	--- the only way back to competitive is disbanding them.
145	function M.disable_blocked_reason()
146	    local marked = storage.team_noncompetitive
147	    if not (marked and next(marked)) then return nil end
148	    local names = {}
149	    for force_name in pairs(marked) do
150	        names[#names + 1] = force_name
151	    end
152	    table.sort(names)
153	    local parts = {}
154	    for _, force_name in ipairs(names) do
155	        parts[#parts + 1] = helpers.team_tag_with_leader(force_name)
156	    end
157	    local plural = #parts > 1
158	    return "Cannot return to competitive mode: " .. table.concat(parts, ", ")
159	        .. (plural and " have" or " has")
160	        .. " played with team modifiers and " .. (plural and "are" or "is")
161	        .. " marked non-competitive. The mark clears only when the team disbands."
162	end
163	
164	--- Remove every team's modifiers and restore standard settings. Called when
165	--- the admin turns non-competitive mode off — normally a no-op, since the
166	--- disable is blocked while any modifier is active (disable_blocked_reason);
167	--- kept as a belt-and-braces cleanup should the two ever disagree.
168	function M.revert_all()
169	    if not storage.team_modifiers or not next(storage.team_modifiers) then
170	        storage.team_modifiers = nil
171	        return
172	    end
173	    local names = {}
174	    for force_name in pairs(storage.team_modifiers) do
175	        names[#names + 1] = force_name
176	    end
177	    storage.team_modifiers = nil
178	    storage.team_noncompetitive = nil
179	    for _, force_name in ipairs(names) do
180	        apply_team(force_name)   -- entry gone -> reverts to standard
181	    end
182	    helpers.broadcast(
183	        "All team modifiers removed — every team is back on standard settings.")
184	end
185	
186	--- Drop a released slot's modifiers, non-competitive mark, and surface
187	--- state, so a future team reusing the slot never inherits an old handicap.
188	--- Disbanding is the ONE path that clears the mark.
189	function M.on_release(force_name)
190	    if storage.team_noncompetitive then
191	        storage.team_noncompetitive[force_name] = nil
192	    end
193	    if not entry(force_name) then return end
194	    storage.team_modifiers[force_name] = nil
195	    apply_team(force_name)
196	end
197	
198	-- ─── Display helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
199	
200	--- One-line description of a team's modifiers ("Peaceful biters", comma-
201	--- separated when more exist), or nil when the team is standard.
202	function M.describe(force_name)
203	    local e = entry(force_name)
204	    if not (e and next(e)) then return nil end
205	    local parts = {}
206	    for _, def in ipairs(M.MODIFIERS) do
207	        if e[def.key] then parts[#parts + 1] = def.label end
208	    end
209	    return table.concat(parts, ", ")
210	end
211	
212	--- HUD tag under the top-bar clock: "non-competitive", with the team's own
213	--- modifiers appended ("non-competitive · peaceful") so an asymmetry is
214	--- visible at a glance. nil when the mode is off.
215	function M.hud_tag(force_name)
216	    if not M.is_active() then return nil end
217	    local caption = "non-competitive"
218	    local shorts  = {}
219	    for _, def in ipairs(M.MODIFIERS) do
220	        if M.has(force_name, def.key) then shorts[#shorts + 1] = def.short end
221	    end
222	    if #shorts > 0 then
223	        caption = caption .. " · " .. table.concat(shorts, " · ")
224	    end
225	    local mine = M.describe(force_name) or "standard settings"
226	    return caption,
227	        "This server allows per-team modifiers.\nThis team: " .. mine
228	            .. "\n" .. guidance()
229	end
230	
231	--- Modifier line for a Teams GUI card, or nil when the team is standard
232	--- (or the mode is off).
233	function M.card_line(force_name)
234	    if not M.is_active() then return nil end
235	    local e = entry(force_name)
236	    if not (e and next(e)) then return nil end
237	    local caps, tips = {}, {}
238	    for _, def in ipairs(M.MODIFIERS) do
239	        if e[def.key] then
240	            caps[#caps + 1] = def.icon .. " " .. def.label
241	            tips[#tips + 1] = def.tooltip
242	        end
243	    end
244	    return table.concat(caps, "   "),
245	        table.concat(tips, "\n") .. "\n(non-competitive team modifier)"
246	end
247	
248	--- Orange badge shown next to a marked team's name (admin GUI,
249	--- /mts-modifiers), or nil for unmarked teams.
250	function M.marked_badge(force_name)
251	    if not M.is_marked(force_name) then return nil end
252	    return "[color=1,0.65,0][non-competitive][/color]"
253	end
254	
255	--- Prefix for record/milestone broadcasts: tagged while the mode is on, so
256	--- awards earned under uneven rules carry a visible asterisk.
257	function M.records_tag()
258	    return M.is_active() and "[Records | non-competitive]" or "[Records]"
259	end
260	
261	--- Chat notice for players joining a non-competitive server.
262	function M.print_mode_notice(player)
263	    if not M.is_active() then return end
264	    player.print("[color=1,0.65,0]This server is running in NON-COMPETITIVE"
265	        .. " mode — teams may play under different settings. " .. guidance()
266	        .. "[/color]")
267	end
268	
269	return M
270

28	--- ok=true, err=nil means the rename was applied OR was a no-op (name unchanged).
29	--- ok=false, err=<message> means it was rejected; the caller prints the message.
30	function rename.attempt(player, raw_text)
31	    if not (player and player.valid) then return false, nil end
32	    local force_name = player.force and player.force.name
33	    if not (force_name and force_name:find("^team%-")) then
34	        return false, "You are not on a team yet."
35	    end
36	    if not force_utils.is_team_leader(player) then
37	        return false, "Only the team leader can rename the team."
38	    end
39	
40	    local new_name = (raw_text or ""):match("^%s*(.-)%s*$")
41	    if new_name == "" then
42	        return false, "Team name cannot be empty."
43	    end
44	    local max_len = team_settings.MAX_TEAM_NAME_LEN or 16
45	    if #new_name > max_len then
46	        return false, "Team name is too long (max " .. max_len .. " characters)."
47	    end
48	    if new_name == helpers.display_name(force_name) then
49	        return true  -- unchanged: no-op, no broadcast/event
50	    end
51	
52	    storage.team_names = storage.team_names or {}
53	    for fn, nm in pairs(storage.team_names) do
54	        if fn ~= force_name and nm == new_name then
55	            return false, "Another team already uses that name."
56	        end
57	    end
58	
59	    storage.team_names[force_name] = new_name
60	    helpers.broadcast("[Team] " .. helpers.colored_name(player.name, player.chat_color)
61	        .. " renamed their team to " .. helpers.team_tag_with_leader(force_name) .. ".")

69	    awards_gui.update_all()

27	local function force_member_count(force)
28	    local n = 0
29	    for _ in pairs(force.players) do n = n + 1 end
30	    -- A member currently spectating is on the "spectator" force, so absent from
31	    -- force.players. Count them too, or a disband/leave decision undercounts and

33	    for idx, real in pairs(storage.spectator_real_force or {}) do

50	local function copy_force_state(source, target)
51	    for name, tech in pairs(source.technologies) do
52	        if tech.researched then
53	            local t = target.technologies[name]
54	            if t and not t.researched then t.researched = true end
55	        end
56	    end
57	    for _, quality in pairs({"uncommon", "rare", "epic", "legendary"}) do
58	        pcall(function()
59	            if source.is_quality_unlocked(quality) then target.unlock_quality(quality) end
60	        end)
61	    end
62	    if source.is_space_platforms_unlocked() then
63	        pcall(target.unlock_space_platforms)

96	local function strip_team_from_records(records_table, team)
97	    if not records_table then return end
98	    for key, entry in pairs(records_table) do
99	        -- Drop this team's own leaderboard slice so a recycled slot (which reuses
100	        -- the same "team-N" force name) can record its OWN completion instead of
101	        -- inheriting the previous occupant's frozen entry (records.update refuses
102	        -- to overwrite an existing entries[force_name]).
103	        if entry.entries then entry.entries[team] = nil end
104	
105	        -- If the leaver held first and/or fastest, recompute them from the
106	        -- SURVIVING entries rather than nil-ing the whole record key -- the old
107	        -- code destroyed every other team's entry for this achievement when the
108	        -- leaver held both. "first" here becomes "earliest surviving team" (the
109	        -- true first-achiever is genuinely gone once its slot recycles).
110	        local held = (entry.first   and entry.first.team   == team)
111	                  or (entry.fastest and entry.fastest.team == team)
112	        if held then
113	            local first, fastest
114	            for _, e in pairs(entry.entries or {}) do
115	                if not first   or e.tick    < first.tick      then first   = e end
116	                if not fastest or e.elapsed < fastest.elapsed then fastest = e end
117	            end
118	            entry.first, entry.fastest = first, fastest
119	        end
120	
121	        -- Drop the key only when nothing remains (no surviving entries and no
122	        -- first/fastest -- the latter guards pre-leaderboard saves whose entries
123	        -- table was never populated).
124	        if not (entry.first or entry.fastest or (entry.entries and next(entry.entries))) then
125	            records_table[key] = nil
126	        end
127	    end
128	end

139	    storage.team_slot_generation   = {}

141	    for i = 1, max do
142	        local force_name = "team-" .. i
143	        local ok, new_force = pcall(game.create_force, force_name)
144	        if not ok then
145	            log("[multi-team-support] WARNING: Could not create " .. force_name
146	                .. " (64 force limit reached)")
147	            break
148	        end
149	        copy_force_state(game.forces.player, new_force)
150	        for _, other_force in pairs(game.forces) do
151	            if other_force.name ~= "enemy" and other_force ~= new_force
152	               and not INTERNAL_TURRET_FORCES[other_force.name] then
153	                new_force.set_cease_fire(other_force, true)
154	                other_force.set_cease_fire(new_force, true)
155	            end
156	        end
157	        -- Share chart data with the built-in player force (no active members
158	        -- in MTS, but sharing its chart is desirable). Also set by
159	        -- reset_force_state on every claim/release cycle.
